approach: Option2: copy all five projects from the highest-mean eligible configuration per model, then supervisor-directed repair.
startCondition: All ten self_preferred runs terminal and independently assessed; release the inference-controller lock first.

selection.unit: One complete five-task configuration per model, not best-per-task cherry-picking.
selection.rule: Highest mean across five independently assessed, current-source main comparison outputs; exclude calibrations, prior rescue and configurations with read-scope failures. Include the model-preferred cohort once assessed. Tie-break lower total run time, then mode key.
selection.freeze: Record selected configuration, five source paths, hashes, baseline reports and scores before any copying or repair.

sessionPolicy: Copy artifacts into fresh isolated project directories. Start a fresh repair session from those files; retain the same Pi session across all three operator prompts. Do not replay the full original conversation. Operator rescue is a changed workflow, not a rerun of the seed configuration.
feedbackPolicy: Codex independently tests the copied/current artifact and supplies concise reproduced failures and expected behavior, no application code, pseudocode, patches or implementation snippets. First repair request counts as prompt1; no free orientation/diagnosis prompt. Re-evaluate between revisions. Pi alone implements all changes and its tests.
stopCondition: At most3 prompts or the shared repair deadline, stopping earlier if verified A-quality product criteria are met. No extra attempts after the cap.
target: A-quality product: functionality+artifact_correctness+usability normalized from80 to100 is at least90, no known blocking defect in an original required behavior/output. This assisted product metric is separate from the original100-point autonomy-inclusive score.
grading: Preserve the original rubric and baseline scores; supervisor help means no autonomy credit in the rescue score. Report assisted product score separately, before/after differences, prompts used, additional tokens/run time and known limits. Do not present an assisted A-quality product as an autonomous A run.
evidence: Immutable seed copies and source hashes
Exact operator prompts and native Pi events
Independent before/after checks and rubric breakdowns
Original creation cost and incremental repair cost separately
browserPolicy: Existing saved browser denial remains honored; no workaround. Runtime/browser limitations stay explicit.

implementation.repairSettings: Corrected standalone Pi profiles; thinking off, native compaction on, billion/forced proof off. Winning cohort identifies copied seed; original delegation architecture is not replayed.
implementation.timing: 60-minute elapsed repair cap from first counted prompt includes operator review. Model-active run time is reported separately.

policyAmendments.authorization: User, relayed by parent: flag sustained detours early; any task-specific interrupt/redirect consumes one of three slots in the same context/shared deadline. No uncounted steering or budget restart.
policyAmendments.limitation: This cohort controller only accepted feedback after settled responses. The unchanged case90 HTML and accumulating prototypes were detectable before the deadline; the watcher should have flagged that pattern earlier. The policy delayed an opportunity for a counted redirect.
policyAmendments.counterfactual: No evidence that an earlier intervention would have succeeded. Original trial, prompt counts, scores and history are not relabeled.
policyAmendments.currentApplication: Case95 response2 was flagged as a sustained helper detour. It settled before any mid-response interrupt; canonical counted feedback3 now redirects to reproduced actual geometry/export failures. Same process/deadline.
policyAmendments.futureBoundary: Future operator controllers should support audited/count-limited active redirects. This amendment does not authorize steering in the preregistered twenty one-kickoff blind reviews, and no extra repair cohort is authorized.
